title: Billing Manual, Monthly Statement Chapter — Utility Pass-Through Service Charges by Service
content:
This chapter states how the monthly Utility Pass-Through Service statement is built. Figures named here (read day, statement day, due period, rates, fixed charges, administration fee) are the schedule's own figures.

## 1. Read cycle and statement

Every submeter is read on the schedule's meter read day, and consumption between consecutive reads is billed on the statement issued on the statement day of the following month and due the schedule's payment-due number of calendar days after the statement date.

## 2. Water — retired clause

The former clause "Water is billed by block on the cycle's consumption: the part up to the first-block bound at the first-block rate, the part above that up to the second-block bound at the second-block rate, and the rest at the third-block rate, plus the water base charge" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the water usage charge.

## 3. Sewer

Where sewer is metered on water, it is billed at the sewer rate on the cycle's water consumption up to the sewer monthly cap, plus the sewer base charge. Where sewer is a flat fee, it is the sewer flat fee.

## 4. Natural gas, propane and electricity

Natural gas is billed at the gas rate plus the gas base charge, and propane at the propane rate plus the propane base charge. Electricity is billed at the first-tier rate up to the first-tier bound and at the second-tier rate above it, plus the electric customer charge.

## 5. Trash and the flat-rate schedule

Trash is the trash flat fee. On the flat-rate schedule, water, sewer and trash together are the single flat utility fee, billed for the calendar month with no meter reads.

## 6. Proration

Fixed charges are prorated on the actual days in the period, in the opening and final periods only: the monthly amount divided by the days in the cycle, times the days of service. Consumption charges are never prorated.

## 7. Administration fee and rounding

Each statement carries one administration fee, including the final statement, and each computed charge is rounded half up to the cent.

## 8. Services not billed

A charge is posted for a service only when the schedule bills that service.

## Worked examples (hypothetical consumption, schedule figures from the rate sheets)

| Charge | Inputs | Working | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metered sewer, Submetered Water & Sewer Schedule | 9.40 kgal of water; cap 8.00 kgal; rate 6.94 | 9.40 is above the cap, so 8.00 kgal is charged; 8.00 times 6.94 is 55.52 | 55.52, with the 12.40 sewer base charge billed as a fixed charge |
| Natural gas, Submetered Water, Sewer & Natural Gas Schedule | 46 ccf; rate 1.182 | 46 times 1.182 is 54.372, rounded half up | 54.37, plus the gas base charge |
| Electricity, Submetered Electric, Water & Sewer Schedule | 1,240 kWh; first tier to 1000 kWh at 0.1284, above at 0.1497 | 1000 times 0.1284 is 128.40; 240 times 0.1497 is 35.928; together 164.328, rounded half up | 164.33, plus the electric customer charge |
| Trash in an opening period | trash flat fee 19.40; 12 days of service in a 30-day cycle | 19.40 divided by 30, times 12, is 7.76 | 7.76 |

## Points of judgement

- **Is a consumption charge reduced because service began mid-cycle?** No. Only fixed charges are prorated, and only in the opening and final periods.
- **Does the final statement carry an administration fee?** Yes, one, like every statement.
- **Is sewer charged on a schedule whose sewer is included in the flat utility fee?** Not as a separate charge; a charge is posted for a service only when the schedule bills that service.
